about: Cut 3 casting, picked by ear by Kai on the voice audition page (https://claude.ai/artifact/PjhfJL9Ne3iFCtV6eXDH6t), 2026-10-20. Prompts are the exact ones that made the picked takes (voice3.py audition). Maddie (bot) stays Aoede, Bristol.

woman.name: Sandra
woman.prompt:
# AUDIO PROFILE
Sandra, a working-class woman from Bolton, Lancashire in her fifties, married to Derek for thirty years.

## THE SCENE
A tiled lavatory in a Cold War bunker under a hill, five years underground with a hundred people and one toilet. Echo off the tiles.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: sharp, sarcastic, every line a jab; not shouting at first, then loud. Funny because she is completely serious.
Pace: quick and clipped, a pause before 'Again.'
Accent: Northern English, as heard in Lancashire, around Bolton. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the wife in a British sitcom row that the whole street can hear.

man.name: Derek
man.prompt:
# AUDIO PROFILE
Derek, a working-class man from Liverpool in his fifties, Sandra's husband.

## THE SCENE
A tiled lavatory in a Cold War bunker, then a circle of a hundred survivors being asked to trust the machine that killed everyone. Echo off the tiles.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: indignant and exasperated in the row, arms-in-the-air disbelief; in the circle, angry and frightened, the first one to say no.
Pace: bursts, getting louder.
Accent: Scouse, as heard in Liverpool. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the bloke in a British sitcom who is losing an argument and knows it.

lady.name: The old lady
lady.prompt:
# AUDIO PROFILE
The old lady: an Englishwoman of the old school in her eighties who has run the bunker's kitchen for five years and is frightened of nothing.

## THE SCENE
The corridor just inside the bunker's blast doors, smoke still drifting in; later the canteen, a hundred people in a circle.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: dry, flat, deeply suspicious at first, then the softest she ever gets ('Kettle's on'); in the circle, matter-of-fact and very funny without trying.
Pace: slow and deliberate, long pauses she is in no hurry to fill.
Accent: old-fashioned Received Pronunciation, as heard on the BBC in the 1950s; clipped, precise, Home Counties. Never American.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the formidable grandmother in a British drama who everyone, including the robot, does what she says.
